commands.details:
查询打卡结果

Risk: write

Full parameter schema:
  lark-cli schema attendance.user_tasks.query

Usage:
  lark-cli attendance user_tasks query [flags]

API Parameters:
  Required:
      --employee-type string   员工ID类型。如果没有后台管理权限，可使用通过手机号或邮箱获取用户 ID. enum: employee_id=员工 employee ID，即飞书管理后台 > 组织架构 > 成员与部门...|employee_no=员工工号，即飞书管理后台 > 组织架构 > 成员与部门 > 成员详情中的工号
  Optional:
      --ignore-invalid-users      是否忽略无效和没有权限的用户，对应employee_type。如果 true，则返回有效用户的信息，并告知无效和没.... bool flag (presence = true; omit for false; takes no value)
      --include-terminated-user   由于新入职员工可以复用已离职员工的 employee_no/employee_id，对应employee_type.... bool flag (presence = true; omit for false; takes no value)

Request Body:
      --data string   JSON request body. Supports - and @file.

Raw Parameter Input:
      --params string   Raw URL/query params JSON. Supports - and @file. If both set, typed flags override matching keys in --params.

Execution:
      --as string   identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run     print request without executing

Output:
      --format string   output format: json|ndjson|table|csv (default json)
  -q, --jq string       jq expression to filter JSON output
  -o, --output string   output file path for binary responses

Other:
  -h, --help   help for query
      --json   shorthand for --format json

employee_type.description: 员工ID类型。如果没有后台管理权限，可使用[通过手机号或邮箱获取用户 ID](https://open.feishu.cn/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/reference/contact-v3/user/batch_get_id)
enumDescriptions: 员工 employee ID，即[飞书管理后台](https://example.feishu.cn/admin/contacts/departmentanduser) > 组织架构 > 成员与部门 > 成员详情中的用户 ID
员工工号，即[飞书管理后台](https://example.feishu.cn/admin/contacts/departmentanduser) > 组织架构 > 成员与部门 > 成员详情中的工号

ignore_invalid_users.description: 是否忽略无效和没有权限的用户，对应employee_type。如果 true，则返回有效用户的信息，并告知无效和没有权限的用户信息；如果 false，且 user_ids 中存在无效或没有权限的用户，则返回错误 （暂不支持该字段）

include_terminated_user.description: 由于新入职员工可以复用已离职员工的 employee_no/employee_id，对应employee_type。如果 true，则返回 employee_no/employee_id 对应的所有在职 + 离职员工的数据；如果 false，则只返回 employee_no/employee_id 对应的在职或最近一个离职员工的数据

check_date_from.description: 查询的起始工作日，格式为yyyyMMdd

check_date_to.description: 查询的结束工作日，格式为yyyyMMdd

need_overtime_result.description: 是否需要加班班段打卡结果；当need_overtime_result=true时，会返回加班班段，加班班段通过task_shift_type=1标识，加班班段上下班与正常班段相连时会出现共用record_id情况。例如：9-18为正常班次，18-19为加班班次，打卡结果中records 会出现两段，分别为9-18，18-19 且两段上下班record_id相同（check_in_record_id和check_out_record_id相同）。非相连加班班次正常分段返回。当need_overtime_result=false时，仅返回正常班段且task_shift_type=0

user_ids.description: employee_no 或 employee_id 列表，对应employee_type，长度不超过 50

    • lark-cli base +dashboard-block-create --base-token <base_token> --dashboard-id <dashboard_id> --name "Order Count" --type statistics --data-config '{"table_name":"Orders","count_all":true}'

    • data_config uses table and field names, not table_id or field_id.
    • Read dashboard-block-data-config.md as the SSOT for chart templates, filters, metric rules, and type-specific fields; do not invent data_config from natural language.

commands.details:
Batch create records

Usage:
  lark-cli base +record-batch-create [flags]

Flags:
      --as string           identity type: user | bot
      --base-token string   base token
      --dry-run             print request without executing
      --format string       output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                help for +record-batch-create
  -q, --jq string           jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json string         batch create JSON object, e.g. {"fields":["Name","Status"],"rows":[["Task A","Todo"],["Task B",null]]}; rows follow fields order
      --table-id string     table ID (must start with tbl if ID) or name

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Happy path fields: fields is the column order; rows is an array of row arrays; each row must match fields order and may use null for empty cells.
    • Before writing, use +field-list to confirm real writable fields; do not write system fields, formula, lookup, or attachment fields as normal CellValue.
    • Batch create supports max 200 rows per call.
    • After batch-creating known helper rows, use the returned record IDs and your submitted rows; do not immediately +record-list the same table unless you need server-normalized formula/lookup values or failure diagnosis.
    • Use the record-batch-create guide for command limits and edge cases.
    • CellValue happy path: text/phone/url -> "text"; number/currency/percent/rating -> 12.5; select -> "Todo"; multi-select -> ["Tag A","Tag B"]; datetime -> "2026-03-24 10:00:00"; checkbox -> true/false.
    • ID-based CellValue: user/group/link fields use arrays like [{"id":"ou_xxx"}], [{"id":"oc_xxx"}], [{"id":"rec_xxx"}]; location uses {"lng":116.397428,"lat":39.90923}; null clears a cell when allowed.
    • Do not guess user/chat/linked-record IDs or location coordinates; resolve them first with the relevant contact/im/record lookup flow.
    • Use lark-base-cell-value.md for complex CellValue shapes and special field types; do not invent values for fields not covered by the happy path.

commands.details:
Search records in a table

Usage:
  lark-cli base +record-search [flags]

Flags:
      --base-token string          base token
      --table-id string            table ID (must start with tbl if ID) or name
      --json string                record search JSON object for the full request body, e.g. {"keyword":"Alice","search_fields":["Name"],"select_fields":["Name","Status"],"filter":{"logic":"and","conditions":[]},"sort":[{"field":"Updated","desc":true}],"limit":50}; escape hatch for advanced cases
      --keyword string             keyword for record search; required unless --json is used
      --search-field stringArray   field ID or name to search; repeat for multiple fields; required unless --json is used
      --field-id stringArray       field ID or name to include; repeat to project only needed fields
      --view-id string             view ID or name; omit for reading all table records, or set to read a user-specified or temporary filtered/sorted view
      --filter-json string         filter JSON object or @file, same shape as view filter JSON; overrides --view-id view filters (supports @file)
      --sort-json string           sort JSON array or @file, e.g. [{"field":"Updated","desc":true}]; also accepts {"sort_config":[...]}; order is priority; max 10 (supports @file)
      --offset int                 pagination offset
      --limit int                  pagination size, range 1-200 (default 10)
      --format string              output format: markdown (default) | json (markdown|json) (default "markdown")
      --dry-run                    print request without executing
  -q, --jq string                  jq expression to filter JSON output
      --as string                  identity type: user | bot
  -h, --help                       help for +record-search

Risk: read

Tips:
    • Happy path fields: keyword (string), search_fields (1-20 field names/ids), select_fields (optional projection, <=50), view_id (optional), offset (default 0), limit (default 10, range 1-200).
    • JSON constraints: keyword length >=1; search_fields length 1-20; select_fields length <=50; offset >=0 defaults to 0; limit range 1-200 defaults to 10.
    • view_id scopes search to records in that view; when select_fields is omitted, returned fields follow that view's visible fields.
    • Example: lark-cli base +record-search --base-token <base_token> --table-id <table_id> --keyword Alice --search-field Name --field-id Name --field-id Status --limit 20
    • Example with filter/sort JSON: lark-cli base +record-search --base-token <base_token> --table-id <table_id> --keyword Alice --search-field Name --filter-json @filter.json --sort-json '[{"field":"Updated","desc":true}]'
    • Text equality filter: --filter-json '{"logic":"and","conditions":[["Title","==","Launch plan"]]}'
    • Text contains/like filter: --filter-json '{"logic":"and","conditions":[["Title","intersects","urgent"]]}'
    • Option intersection filter: --filter-json '{"logic":"and","conditions":[["Tags","intersects",["P0","Blocked"]]]}'
    • Sort priority follows --sort-json array order.
    • Query priority: --filter-json overrides --view-id's view filter JSON; --sort-json overrides --view-id's view sort config.
    • Use +record-search for keyword matching; use --filter-json for structured conditions and --sort-json for result ordering.
    • Use --json only when you need to pass the full search body directly.
    • Default output is markdown; pass --format json to get the raw JSON envelope.

commands.details:
Create or update a record

Usage:
  lark-cli base +record-upsert [flags]

Flags:
      --as string           identity type: user | bot
      --base-token string   base token
      --dry-run             print request without executing
      --format string       output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                help for +record-upsert
  -q, --jq string           jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json string         record field map JSON object, e.g. {"Name":"Alice","Status":"Todo"}; do not wrap in fields
      --record-id string    record ID
      --table-id string     table ID (must start with tbl if ID) or name

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Happy path JSON is a top-level field map: each key is a real field name or field ID, each value is that field's CellValue.
    • Without --record-id this creates a record; with --record-id this updates that record. It does not auto-upsert by business key.
    • Before writing, use +field-list to confirm real writable fields; do not write system fields, formula, lookup, or attachment fields as normal CellValue.
    • Use the record-upsert guide for command limits and edge cases.
    • CellValue happy path: text/phone/url -> "text"; number/currency/percent/rating -> 12.5; select -> "Todo"; multi-select -> ["Tag A","Tag B"]; datetime -> "2026-03-24 10:00:00"; checkbox -> true/false.
    • ID-based CellValue: user/group/link fields use arrays like [{"id":"ou_xxx"}], [{"id":"oc_xxx"}], [{"id":"rec_xxx"}]; location uses {"lng":116.397428,"lat":39.90923}; null clears a cell when allowed.
    • Do not guess user/chat/linked-record IDs or location coordinates; resolve them first with the relevant contact/im/record lookup flow.
    • Use lark-base-cell-value.md for complex CellValue shapes and special field types; do not invent values for fields not covered by the happy path.

Risk: read

  • Fetch one user's profile by id, or your own with --user-id omitted. Use it under bot identity — `+search-user` is user-only.

commands.details:
Search Lark/Feishu users by keyword, open_id list, or filter (requires --as user)

Risk: read

When to use:
  • The primary user lookup for user identity: search by keyword or email, resolve known ids with --user-ids, or get yourself with --user-ids me — it does by-id reads too, so as a user you rarely need `+get-user`. Each match returns an open_id and p2p_chat_id to chain into follow-ups.

Avoid when:
  • Running as a bot — this shortcut is user-only; use `+get-user` instead (it supports bot identity)
  • You only need users' personal status for ids you already hold → use `user_profiles batch_query`

Tips:
  • Filter-only enumeration — users you've chatted with: lark-cli contact +search-user --has-chatted
  • Refine same-name hits: lark-cli contact +search-user --query '张三' --has-chatted --exclude-external-users
  • Multi-name fanout: lark-cli contact +search-user --queries 'alice,bob,张三'
  • on has_more=true add filters or tighten --query — there is no auto-pagination.

Examples:
  • Find a user by name
      lark-cli contact +search-user --query "alice" --as user
  • Fetch known users by open_id (me = yourself)
      lark-cli contact +search-user --user-ids "ou_3a8b****6a7b,me" --as user

Related skills (read for end-to-end usage):
  lark-cli skills read lark-contact
  lark-cli skills read lark-contact/references/lark-contact-search-user.md

Usage:
  lark-cli contact +search-user [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                identity type: user
      --dry-run                  print request without executing
      --exclude-external-users   exclude external (cross-tenant) users; default includes them (omit to disable; =false rejected)
      --format string            output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
      --has-chatted              restrict to users you've chatted with (omit to disable; =false rejected)
      --has-enterprise-email     restrict to users with enterprise email (omit to disable; =false rejected)
  -h, --help                     help for +search-user
  -q, --jq string                jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                     shorthand for --format json
      --lang string              override locale for localized_name (e.g. zh_cn, en_us)

      --page-size int            rows per request, 1-30 (default 20)
      --queries string           comma-separated keywords searched in parallel; output is a flat users[] with matched_query plus a queries[] sidecar
      --query string             search keyword (≤ 50 characters)
      --user-ids string          open_ids to look up or restrict --query against (CSV; me = caller; ≤ 100)

commands.details:
批量获取用户个人资料（个人状态、个性签名）。Identity: `user` only (`user_access_token`).

Risk: read

When to use:
  • Bulk-fetch personal status and signature for user ids you already have.

Avoid when:
  • Need more than status/signature (name, dept, email), or don't have the open_id yet → use `+search-user`

Tips:
  • Off by default — set include_personal_status / include_description to true under query_option
  • ids in user_ids must match --user-id-type (default open_id)

Examples:
  • Bulk-query status and signature
      lark-cli contact user_profiles batch_query --data '{"user_ids":["ou_3a8b****6a7b"],"query_option":{"include_personal_status":true,"include_description":true}}'

Full parameter schema:
  lark-cli schema contact.user_profiles.batch_query

Related skills (read for end-to-end usage):
  lark-cli skills read lark-contact

Execution:
      --as string   identity type: user | bot

Output:

commands.details:
Add a collaborator/member permission to a Drive document, file, folder, or wiki node

Usage:
  lark-cli drive +member-add [flags]

Flags:
      --as string            identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run              print request without executing
      --format string        output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                 help for +member-add
  -q, --jq string            jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                 shorthand for --format json
      --member-id string     collaborator ID; comma-separated for batch (max 10). Interpretation is decided by --member-type
      --member-kind string   request body type when --member-type=wikispaceid; one of wiki_space_member|wiki_space_viewer|wiki_space_editor
      --member-type string   ID type for --member-id; supported: email|openid|unionid|openchat|opendepartmentid|groupid|appid|wikispaceid
      --need-notification    send an in-app notification after the grant (user identity only)
      --perm string          permission role to grant; defaults to view
      --perm-type string     wiki permission scope; defaults to container; rejected for non-wiki types
      --token string         target token or document URL; type is auto-inferred from URL path when omitted
      --type string          target resource type; required when --token is a bare token
      --yes                  confirm high-risk operation

Risk: high-risk-write

Tips:
    • Resource type is auto-inferred from URL paths; pass --type when --token is a bare token.
    • Supported --member-type values: email, openid, unionid, openchat, opendepartmentid, groupid, appid, wikispaceid.
    • When --member-type=wikispaceid, pass --member-kind wiki_space_member, wiki_space_viewer, or wiki_space_editor.
    • --member-type is required; if the ID prefix conflicts with --member-type (e.g. ou_xxx with email), the command rejects it.
    • --perm defaults to view (safest); use --dry-run first when granting edit or full_access.
    • For wiki nodes, --perm-type defaults to container (current page and sub-pages), except --member-type=wikispaceid where --member-kind provides the wiki-space role.
    • Department collaborator (--member-type=opendepartmentid) requires --as user; bot identity is not supported for department authorization.

commands.details:
Search Lark docs, Wiki, and spreadsheet files with flat filters (Search v2: doc_wiki/search)

Usage:
  lark-cli drive +search [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                     identity type: user | bot
      --chat-ids string               comma-separated chat IDs
      --commented-since string        start of [my commented] time window
      --commented-until string        end of [my commented] time window
      --created-by-me                 restrict to docs originally created by me (uses current user's open_id as original_creator_ids)
      --created-since string          start of [document created] time window
      --created-until string          end of [document created] time window
      --creator-ids string            comma-separated owner open_ids (API field is creator_ids but matched by owner); mutually exclusive with --mine
      --doc-types string              comma-separated types: doc,sheet,bitable,mindnote,file,wiki,docx,folder,catalog,slides,shortcut
      --dry-run                       print request without executing
      --edited-since string           start of [my edited] time window (e.g. 7d, 1m, 1y, 2026-04-01, RFC3339, unix seconds)
      --edited-until string           end of [my edited] time window
      --folder-tokens string          comma-separated folder tokens (doc-only; mutually exclusive with --space-ids)
      --format string                 output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                          help for +search
  -q, --jq string                     jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                          shorthand for --format json
      --mine                          restrict to docs I own (server-side owner semantic, NOT original creator; uses current user's open_id)
      --only-comment                  search comments only
      --only-title                    match titles only
      --opened-since string           start of [my opened] time window
      --opened-until string           end of [my opened] time window
      --original-creator-ids string   comma-separated original creator open_ids; mutually exclusive with --created-by-me
      --page-size string              page size (1-20, default 15) (default "15")
      --page-token string             pagination token from a previous response
      --query string                  search keyword (may be empty to browse by filter only); max 30 characters by Unicode code point (CJK counts 1 each), over 30 the server rejects with 99992402 field validation failed
      --sharer-ids string             comma-separated sharer open_ids
      --sort string                   sort type (default|edit_time|edit_time_asc|open_time|create_time)
      --space-ids string              comma-separated wiki space IDs (wiki-only; mutually exclusive with --folder-tokens)

Risk: read

Tips:
    • Time flags accept relative (e.g. 7d, 1m, 1y), absolute (2026-04-01, RFC3339), or unix seconds.
    • my_edit_time and my_comment_time are hour-aggregated server-side; sub-hour inputs are snapped and a notice is printed to stderr.
    • Use --created-by-me for "docs I created". Use --mine for "docs I own" (owner semantic).
    • --folder-tokens limits to doc-only search; --space-ids limits to wiki-only. They cannot be combined.

created-by-me.description: to docs originally created by me (uses current user's open_id as original_creator_ids)

creator-ids.description: comma-separated owner open_ids (API field is creator_ids but matched by owner); mutually exclusive with --mine

commands.details:
Upload a local file to Drive

Usage:
  lark-cli drive +upload [flags]

Flags:
      --as string             identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run               print request without executing
      --file string           local file path (files > 20MB use multipart upload automatically)
      --file-token string     existing file token to overwrite in place
      --folder-token string   target folder token (default: root folder; mutually exclusive with --wiki-token)
      --format string         output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                  help for +upload
  -q, --jq string             jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                  shorthand for --format json
      --name string           uploaded file name (default: local file name)
      --wiki-token string     target wiki node token (uploads under that wiki node; mutually exclusive with --folder-token)

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Omit both --folder-token and --wiki-token to upload into the caller's Drive root folder.
    • Use --wiki-token <wiki_node_token> to upload under a wiki node; the shortcut maps this to parent_type=wiki automatically.
    • Pass --file-token <file_token> to overwrite an existing Drive file in place; the shortcut forwards file_token to the upload API.
    • In bot mode, automatic full_access (可管理权限) grant only applies to newly uploaded files; overwrite via --file-token does not modify existing file permissions.

      --page-all                automatically paginate through all pages (capped by --page-limit)

标识一个用户在某个应用中的身份。同一个用户在不同应用中的 Open ID 不同。[了解更多：如何获取 Open ID？](/ssl:ttdoc/uAjLw4CM/ugTN1YjL4UTN24CO1UjN/trouble-shooting/how-to-obtain-openid)
飞书开放平台应用的唯一标识。在创建应用时，由系统自动生成，用户不能自行修改。[了解更多：如何获取应用的 App ID？](/ssl:ttdoc/uAjLw4CM/ugTN1YjL4UTN24CO1UjN/trouble-shooting/how-to-obtain-app-id)

id_list.description: 成员 ID 列表。ID 类型与查询参数 member_id_type 的取值一致。; - 移除群内的用户时推荐使用 OpenID，获取方式可参考文档[如何获取 Open ID？](https://open.feishu.cn/document/uAjLw4CM/ugTN1YjL4UTN24CO1UjN/trouble-shooting/how-to-obtain-openid)。;- 移除群内的机器人时需填写应用的 App ID，请参考[如何获取应用的 App ID？](https://open.feishu.cn/document/uAjLw4CM/ugTN1YjL4UTN24CO1UjN/trouble-shooting/how-to-obtain-app-id)。; 注意：;- 成员列表不可为空。;- 每次请求，最多移除 50 个用户或者 5 个机器人

yes.description: CLI confirmation gate. Must be true to execute; lark-cli rejects with confirmation_required if absent or false. Pass --yes only after the user has explicitly confirmed; not sent to the backend.

commands.details:

Risk: read

Full parameter schema:

Usage:
  lark-cli im chat.members get [flags]

API Parameters:
  Required:
      --chat-id string   群 ID

      --check-security-conf     是否检查安全配置. bool flag (presence = true; omit for false; takes no value)

      --page-size int           分页大小，用来限制一次请求所返回的数据条目数
      --page-token string       分页标记，第一次请求不填，表示从头开始遍历

Raw Parameter Input:

Execution:
      --as string        identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run          print request without executing
      --page-all         automatically paginate through all pages
      --page-delay int   delay in ms between pages (default 200)
      --page-limit int   max pages to fetch with --page-all (0 = unlimited) (default 10)

Output:
      --format string   output format: json|ndjson|table|csv (default json)
  -q, --jq string       jq expression to filter JSON output
  -o, --output string   output file path for binary responses

Other:
  -h, --help   help for get
      --json   shorthand for --format json

commands.details:

commands.details:
获取消息或消息链接中资源文件夹的子文件列表。recursive=false 仅返回给定 file_key 的一层子项（folder 子项带 children_count 提示深度）；recursive=true 返回完整层级树（嵌套 children）。

Risk: read

Full parameter schema:
  lark-cli schema im.files.folder

Usage:
  lark-cli im files folder [flags]

API Parameters:
  Required:
      --file-key string   待浏览子文件的文件夹 file_key
      --srcid string      资源来源 ID。srctype=message 时为消息 ID（om_ 开头，resource 侧解析为内部 ID）

commands.details:
Dismiss the read-receipt request banner on an incoming mail by clearing its READ_RECEIPT_REQUEST label, without sending a receipt. Use when the user wants to silence the prompt but refuse to confirm they have read it. Idempotent — safe to re-run.

Usage:
  lark-cli mail +decline-receipt [flags]

Flags:
      --as string           identity type: user
      --dry-run             print request without executing
      --format string       output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                help for +decline-receipt
  -q, --jq string           jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                shorthand for --format json
      --mailbox string      Mailbox email address that owns the message (default: me).
      --message-id string   Required. Message ID of the incoming mail that requested a read receipt.

Risk: write

commands.details:
Use when updating an existing mail draft without sending it. Prefer this shortcut over calling raw drafts.get or drafts.update directly, because it performs draft-safe MIME read/patch/write editing while preserving unchanged structure, attachments, and headers where possible.

Usage:
  lark-cli mail +draft-edit [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                   identity type: user
      --body string                 Full email body for a complete replacement (set_body). Prefer HTML for rich formatting (bold, lists, links); plain text is also supported. Body type is auto-detected. Use --patch-file with set_reply_body when you need to preserve an existing reply/forward quote block; use --body when you want a full body replacement. Mutually exclusive with --body-file. Cannot be combined with --patch-file body ops.
      --body-file string            Path (relative, within cwd subtree) to a file containing the email body HTML. Mutually exclusive with --body. Size capped at 32 MB. (supports @file)
      --draft-id string             Target draft ID. Required for real edits. It can be omitted only when using the --print-patch-template flag by itself.
      --dry-run                     print request without executing
      --format string               output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
      --from string                 Mailbox email address containing the draft (default: me). Prefer --mailbox for clarity; --from is kept for backward compatibility. (default "me")
  -h, --help                        help for +draft-edit
      --inspect                     Inspect the draft without modifying it. Returns the draft projection including subject, recipients, body summary, has_quoted_content (whether the draft contains a reply/forward quote block), attachments_summary (with part_id and cid for each attachment), and inline_summary. Run this BEFORE editing body to check has_quoted_content: if true, use set_reply_body in --patch-file to preserve the quote; if false, use set_body.
  -q, --jq string                   jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                        shorthand for --format json
      --mailbox string              Mailbox email address that owns the draft (default: falls back to --from, then me). Takes priority over --from when both are set.
      --patch-file string           Advanced edit entry point for body edits, incremental recipient changes, header edits, attachment changes, or inline-image changes. Use --body/--body-file for quick full-body replacement; use --patch-file with set_body/set_reply_body when you need typed body ops, especially set_reply_body to preserve an existing reply/forward quote block. Run --inspect first to check has_quoted_content, then --print-patch-template for the JSON structure. Relative path only.
      --print-patch-template        Print the JSON template and supported operations for the --patch-file flag. Recommended first step before generating a patch file. No draft read or write is performed.
      --remove-event                Remove the calendar event from the draft.
      --request-receipt             Request a read receipt (Message Disposition Notification, RFC 3798) addressed to the draft's sender. Recipient mail clients may prompt the user, send automatically, or silently ignore — delivery of a receipt is not guaranteed. Adds the Disposition-Notification-To header; existing value is overwritten.
      --set-bcc string              Replace the entire Bcc recipient list with the addresses provided here. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Display-name format is supported.
      --set-cc string               Replace the entire Cc recipient list with the addresses provided here. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Display-name format is supported.
      --set-event-end string        Set calendar event end time (ISO 8601).
      --set-event-location string   Set calendar event location.
      --set-event-start string      Set calendar event start time (ISO 8601).
      --set-event-summary string    Set calendar event title. Must be used together with --set-event-start and --set-event-end.
      --set-priority string         Set email priority: high, normal, low. Setting 'normal' removes any existing priority header.
      --set-subject string          Replace the subject with this final value. Use this for full subject replacement, not for appending a fragment to the existing subject.
      --set-to string               Replace the entire To recipient list with the addresses provided here. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Display-name format is supported.
      --show-lint-details           Include lint metadata (lint_applied[] / original_blocked[]) in the envelope. Default: no lint fields are returned to keep the envelope small.

Risk: write

commands.details:
Send one or more existing mail drafts sequentially. Calls POST /drafts/:draft_id/send for each input ID, isolates per-draft failures, and aggregates the results. Use after the drafts have already been created (via the Lark client, +draft-create, or the drafts.create API).

Usage:
  lark-cli mail +draft-send [flags]

Flags:
      --as string          identity type: user
      --draft-id strings   Draft IDs to send; comma-separated or repeat the flag (max 50).
      --dry-run            print request without executing
      --format string      output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help               help for +draft-send
  -q, --jq string          jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json               shorthand for --format json
      --mailbox string     Mailbox email address that owns the drafts (default: me).
      --stop-on-error      Stop at the first recoverable per-draft failure (default: continue and aggregate). Fatal errors (auth, permission, network, mailbox-level quota) always abort immediately regardless of this flag.
      --yes                confirm high-risk operation

Risk: high-risk-write

Send a read-receipt reply for an incoming message that requested one (i.e. carries the READ_RECEIPT_REQUEST label). Body is auto-generated (subject / recipient / send time / read time) to match the Lark client's receipt format — callers cannot customize it, matching the industry norm that read-receipt bodies are system-generated templates, not free-form replies.       --mailbox string      Mailbox email address that owns the receipt reply (default: me).

      --yes                 confirm high-risk operation

Separate multiple addresses with commas. --cc string Optional. Default Cc recipient list. Template name (≤100 chars). --plain-text Mark the template as plain-text mode (is_plain_text_mode=true). Inline images still require HTML content; use only for pure plain-text templates. --subject string Optional. Default subject saved with the template. --template-content string Template body content. commands.details: Update an existing mail template. Supports --inspect (read-only projection), --print-patch-template (prints a JSON skeleton for --patch-file), and flat flags (--set-subject / --set-name / etc). Internally it GETs the template, applies the patch, rewrites local paths to cid: refs, and PUTs a full-replace update (no optimistic locking: last-write-wins). Usage: lark-cli mail +template-update [flags] Flags: --as string identity type: user | bot --attach string Additional non-inline attachment file path(s), comma-separated. Each file is uploaded to Drive and appended to the template's attachments[] in the exact flag order. --dry-run print request without executing --format string output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json") -h, --help help for +template-update --inspect Inspect the template without modifying it. Returns the current template projection (name/subject/addresses/attachments). No write is performed. -q, --jq string jq expression to filter JSON output --json shorthand for --format json --mailbox string Mailbox email address that owns the template (default: me). --patch-file string Path to a JSON patch file (relative path only). Shape is the same as --print-patch-template output. --print-patch-template Print a JSON template describing the supported --patch-file structure. No network call is made. --set-bcc string Replace the Bcc recipient list. Pass --set-bcc="" to clear the list. --set-cc string Replace the Cc recipient list. Pass --set-cc="" to clear the list. --set-name string Replace the template name (≤100 chars). --set-plain-text Set is_plain_text_mode=true. --set-subject string Replace the template subject. --set-template-content string Replace the template body content. Prefer HTML for rich formatting. --set-template-content-file string Replace template body content with the contents of a file (relative path only). Mutually exclusive with --set-template-content. --set-to string Replace the To recipient list. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Pass --set-to="" to clear the list. --template-id string Template ID to update. Required except when using --print-patch-template by itself. Risk: write

commands.details:
Create a Markdown file in Drive

Usage:
  lark-cli markdown +create [flags]

Flags:
      --as string             identity type: user | bot
      --content string        Markdown content (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))
      --dry-run               print request without executing
      --file string           local .md file path
      --folder-token string   target Drive folder token (default: root folder; mutually exclusive with --wiki-token)
      --format string         output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                  help for +create
  -q, --jq string             jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                  shorthand for --format json
      --name string           file name with .md suffix; required with --content, optional with --file
      --wiki-token string     target wiki node token (uploads under that wiki node; mutually exclusive with --folder-token)

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Omit both --folder-token and --wiki-token to create the Markdown file in the caller's Drive root folder.
    • Use --wiki-token <wiki_node_token> to create the Markdown file under a wiki node; the shortcut maps this to parent_type=wiki automatically.
    • --folder-token and --wiki-token also accept full Lark URLs and normalize them to the required token.

commands.details:
Add, update, or delete todo item(s) on a minute

Usage:
  lark-cli minutes +todo [flags]

Flags:
      --as string             identity type: user
      --dry-run               print request without executing
      --format string         output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                  help for +todo
      --is-done               completion flag; required by single add/update
  -q, --jq string             jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                  shorthand for --format json
      --minute-token string   minute token (required)
      --operation string      operation for a single todo (required unless --todos) (add|update|delete)
      --todo string           todo plain-text content; required by single add/update (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))
      --todo-id string        id of an existing todo; required by single update/delete
      --todos string          batch todo_items JSON array; each item has operation add|update|delete (supports @file / @-) (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Single todo: `--operation add --todo "..." --is-done=false`.
    • Batch: `--todos '[{"operation":"add","content":"...","is_done":false}, ...]'` or `--todos @todos.json`.
    • Batch can mix add, update, and delete in one request; array order is preserved in the API body.
    • Update: `--operation update --todo-id <id> --todo "..." --is-done`.
    • Delete: `--operation delete --todo-id <id>`.
    • `content` is plain text only; markdown formatting is not supported.
    • Use `lark-cli minutes +detail --minute-tokens <token> --todo` to read current todos before writing.

commands.details:
Execute a batch of write shortcuts as a single atomic request (rolls back on failure by default).

Usage:
  lark-cli sheets +batch-update [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                  identity type: user | bot
      --continue-on-error          Continue with remaining operations when a sub-operation fails; default false (abort on first failure)
      --dry-run                    print request without executing
      --flag-name string           flag whose schema to print (omit to list introspectable flags); used with --print-schema
      --format string              output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                       help for +batch-update
  -q, --jq string                  jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                       shorthand for --format json
      --operations string          JSON array: [{"shortcut":"+xxx-yyy","input":{...}}, ...]. shortcut uses CLI names; input is that shortcut's flag set — it includes the per-operation sheet locator (sheet_id or sheet_name) but not the spreadsheet token/url (pass that once at the top level via --url/--spreadsheet-token; +batch-update has no top-level --sheet-id). input keys are the shortcut's flags flattened into JSON (e.g. "range":"A11:B12"), not another nested layer. For basic flags use lark-cli sheets <shortcut> --help; for composite JSON flags use --print-schema --flag-name <flag>. Do not pass an explicit operation field. Strict transaction by default, pass --continue-on-error for soft batch; no nesting; executed serially. (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))
      --print-schema               print JSON Schema for a composite flag instead of executing
      --spreadsheet-token string   Spreadsheet locator (independent from per-operation sheet locator)
      --url string                 Spreadsheet locator (independent from per-operation sheet locator)
      --yes                        confirm high-risk operation

Risk: high-risk-write

Tips:
    • Default is strict transaction — any sub-tool failure rolls the whole batch back. Pass --continue-on-error to keep partial successes.
    • Each sub-op is {shortcut, input}. Do NOT pass input.operation (implied by shortcut name) or input.excel_id / input.url (set at the +batch-update top level).

continue-on-error.description: with remaining operations when a sub-operation fails; default false (abort on first failure)

flag-name.description: flag whose schema to print (omit to list introspectable flags); used with --print-schema

operations.description: JSON array: [{"shortcut":"+xxx-yyy","input":{...}}, ...]. shortcut uses CLI names; input is that shortcut's flag set — it includes the per-operation sheet locator (sheet_id or sheet_name) but not the spreadsheet token/url (pass that once at the top level via --url/--spreadsheet-token; +batch-update has no top-level --sheet-id). input keys are the shortcut's flags flattened into JSON (e.g. "range":"A11:B12"), not another nested layer. commands.details:
Resize columns in pixels (NOT Excel char units): --range + --width <px> for one uniform width, --widths '{"A":100,"C:E":120}' for per-column widths in one atomic call, or --type standard to reset (--range is column letters like "A:E" or "C"; no auto for cols).

Usage:
  lark-cli sheets +cols-resize [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                 identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run                   print request without executing
      --flag-name string          flag whose schema to print (omit to list introspectable flags); used with --print-schema
      --format string             output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                      help for +cols-resize
  -q, --jq string                 jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                      shorthand for --format json
      --print-schema              print JSON Schema for a composite flag instead of executing
      --range A:E                 Column closed range to resize; column letters like A:E or `C` (single column). Required for the uniform form (with `--width` or `--type`); omit with the map form (`--widths`)
      --sheet-id --sheet-name     Sheet reference_id (XOR with --sheet-name)
      --sheet-name --sheet-id     Sheet name (XOR with --sheet-id)
      --spreadsheet-token --url   Spreadsheet token (XOR with --url)
      --type pixel                Sizing mode: pixel (requires `--width`) / `standard` (reset to default column width). Passing --width alone is the common form; `--type standard` cannot be combined with `--width` (pixel|standard)
      --url --spreadsheet-token   Spreadsheet URL (XOR with --spreadsheet-token)
      --width --range             Uniform column width in pixels (e.g. 80 / 120 / 200; NOT Excel character units), used with --range. Passing --width implies pixel mode; --type may be omitted (or set to `pixel` — equivalent). For per-column widths use `--widths`
      --widths "A"                Per-column width map — set different widths for many columns in one atomic call. Keys: single column ("A") or closed range (`"C:E"`); values: pixel width (e.g. 80 / 120 / 200) or `"standard"` (reset to default). Units are pixels, NOT Excel character units (px ≈ chars × 8 + 16). Mutually exclusive with `--range` / `--width` / `--type` (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))

Server enforces no item-count cap and no per-item length cap; values containing commas are accepted (they are escape-encoded on the wire). For very large lists prefer `--source-range`. (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))

XOR with `--options`: pass `--options` for an inline list (type=list), pass this for a range reference (type=listFromRange). `--colors` length rule unchanged (≤ source range cell count); `--highlight` / `--multiple` behave the same. commands.details:
Create a pivot object via the manage_*_object tool.

Usage:
  lark-cli sheets +pivot-create [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                              identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run                                print request without executing
      --flag-name string                       flag whose schema to print (omit to list introspectable flags); used with --print-schema
      --format string                          output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                                   help for +pivot-create
  -q, --jq string                              jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                                   shorthand for --format json
      --print-schema                           print JSON Schema for a composite flag instead of executing
      --properties string                      JSON: {"rows":[...],"columns":[...],"values":[...],"filters":[...],"show_row_grand_total":true,"show_col_grand_total":true} (data source goes through --source; do not put source here) (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))
      --range F1                               Pivot table top-left placement (single A1 value, e.g. F1; create only), maps to `properties.range`; placed at the top-left of the target sub-sheet (a newly created one by default) when omitted. It and `--target-position` both express placement but map to different wire fields — avoid passing conflicting values for both.
      --source 'SheetName'!StartCell:EndCell   Pivot table source range (A1 notation; format 'SheetName'!StartCell:EndCell, e.g. `'Sheet1'!A1:D100`)
      --spreadsheet-token --url                Spreadsheet token (XOR with --url)
      --target-position A1                     Top-left cell within the target sub-sheet (A1 notation, e.g. A1); maps to the top-level `target_position`, default `A1` (not sent when the value is A1). It and `--range` both express placement but map to different wire fields — avoid passing conflicting values for both. (default "A1")
      --target-sheet-id --target-sheet-name    Reference_id of the target sub-sheet where the pivot table will be placed (mutually exclusive with --target-sheet-name; takes priority when both given; when both omitted, a new sub-sheet is auto-created to host the pivot — recommended). Distinct from the data-source sheet, which lives inside --source as a 'Sheet'-prefixed A1 reference like 'Sheet1'!A1:D100.
      --target-sheet-name --target-sheet-id    Name of the target sub-sheet where the pivot table will be placed (mutually exclusive with --target-sheet-id; when both omitted, a new sub-sheet is auto-created to host the pivot — recommended). Distinct from the data-source sheet, which lives inside --source as a 'Sheet'-prefixed A1 reference like 'Sheet1'!A1:D100.
      --url --spreadsheet-token                Spreadsheet URL (XOR with --spreadsheet-token)

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Placement: omit --target-sheet-id / --target-sheet-name and the backend auto-creates a fresh sub-sheet for the pivot — zero overwrite risk. This is the default and the recommended path.
    • Only pass --target-sheet-id/-name to land in an existing sheet; if that sheet holds the source data you MUST set --target-position (or --range) outside the data, else the pivot overwrites it and the anchor shows #REF!.
    • Removing a stray pivot is +pivot-delete (get its id from +pivot-list); +cells-clear / +cells-batch-clear only clear cell values/formats and cannot delete the pivot object.

commands.details:
Write a typed table (columns with types + rows) into an existing spreadsheet; numbers and dates stay type-faithful.

Usage:
  lark-cli sheets +table-put [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                 identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run                   print request without executing
      --flag-name string          flag whose schema to print (omit to list introspectable flags); used with --print-schema
      --format string             output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                      help for +table-put
  -q, --jq string                 jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                      shorthand for --format json
      --print-schema              print JSON Schema for a composite flag instead of executing
      --sheets {"sheets":[...]}   Typed table payload (pandas-DataFrame-shaped) as JSON: top-level {"sheets":[...]}, with each array item a sub-sheet `{name, start_cell?, mode?, header?, allow_overwrite?, columns:["colA","colB",...], data:[[...]], dtypes?:{colA:pandasDtype, ...}, formats?:{colA:numberFormat, ...}}` — `name` and the outer `sheets` envelope are both required. Agents typically use `df_to_sheet(df, name)` from `scripts/sheets_df.py` to pack each DataFrame into one item, then wrap the list in `{"sheets":[...]}`. `dtypes` values are pandas dtype strings (`int64`, `float64`, `Int64`, `bool`, `boolean`, `datetime64[ns]`, `object`, ...); the writer maps them to internal string/number/date/bool — omit `dtypes` and a column writes as text (good for raw CSV-shaped data). `formats[col]` is an Excel number_format string (e.g. `#,##0.00`, `0.0%`, `yyyy-mm`); when absent, date columns default to `yyyy-mm-dd` and string columns to text format (`@`). (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))
      --spreadsheet-token --url   Spreadsheet token to write into (XOR with --url)
      --styles {styles:[...]}     Visual operations applied after the typed write, as JSON: top-level {styles:[...]}. Each item corresponds to one written sheet and must include `name`, plus at least one of `cell_styles` / `row_sizes` / `col_sizes` / `cell_merges`. `cell_styles` entries use +cells-set-style fields with a cell range; row/col sizes use dimension ranges plus type/size; merges use cell ranges plus optional merge_type. The styles array length/order/name must match the written sheets in --sheets.sheets. Run `+table-put --print-schema --flag-name styles` for the full cell_styles field schema. (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))
      --url --spreadsheet-token   Spreadsheet URL to write into (XOR with --spreadsheet-token)

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Writes into an existing spreadsheet — pass --url or --spreadsheet-token. To create a new workbook first, use +workbook-create, then point --spreadsheet-token here.
    • Payload sheets are matched to existing sub-sheets by name (created when absent). Date columns take ISO yyyy-mm-dd strings — converted to real dates (serial + date format).
    • --styles applies number formats, colors, merges, and row/col sizes in the same call (same shape as +workbook-create's --styles): one styles item per written sheet, name-matched. Skips the separate +cells-set-style round-trip.

sheets.description: Typed table payload (pandas-DataFrame-shaped) as JSON: top-level {"sheets":[...]}, with each array item a sub-sheet `{name, start_cell?, mode?, header?, allow_overwrite?, columns:["colA","colB",...], data:[[...]], dtypes?:{colA:pandasDtype, ...}, formats?:{colA:numberFormat, ...}}` — `name` and the outer `sheets` envelope are both required. Agents typically use `df_to_sheet(df, name)` from `scripts/sheets_df.py` to pack each DataFrame into one item, then wrap the list in `{"sheets":[...]}`. `dtypes` values are pandas dtype strings (`int64`, `float64`, `Int64`, `bool`, `boolean`, `datetime64[ns]`, `object`, ...); the writer maps them to internal string/number/date/bool — omit `dtypes` and a column writes as text (good for raw CSV-shaped data). `formats[col]` is an Excel number_format string (e.g. `#,##0.00`, `0.0%`, `yyyy-mm`); when absent, date columns default to `yyyy-mm-dd` and string columns to text format (`@`). (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))

spreadsheet-token.description: Spreadsheet token to write into (XOR with --url)

styles.description: Visual operations applied after the typed write, as JSON: top-level {styles:[...]}. Each item corresponds to one written sheet and must include `name`, plus at least one of `cell_styles` / `row_sizes` / `col_sizes` / `cell_merges`. `cell_styles` entries use +cells-set-style fields with a cell range; row/col sizes use dimension ranges plus type/size; merges use cell ranges plus optional merge_type. The styles array length/order/name must match the written sheets in --sheets.sheets. Run `+table-put --print-schema --flag-name styles` for the full cell_styles field schema. (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))

commands.details:
Create a new spreadsheet, optionally pre-filled with untyped --values or typed --sheets (type-faithful one-step create + write).

Usage:
  lark-cli sheets +workbook-create [flags]

Flags:
      --as string               identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run                 print request without executing
      --flag-name string        flag whose schema to print (omit to list introspectable flags); used with --print-schema
      --folder-token string     Target folder token; placed at the drive root when omitted
      --format string           output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                    help for +workbook-create
  -q, --jq string               jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                    shorthand for --format json
      --print-schema            print JSON Schema for a composite flag instead of executing
      --sheets +table-put       Typed table payload as JSON (same shape as +table-put): top-level `{"sheets":[...]}`, with each array item a sub-sheet `{name, start_cell?, mode?, header?, allow_overwrite?, columns:["colA","colB",...], data:[[...]], dtypes?:{colA:pandasDtype, ...}, formats?:{colA:numberFormat, ...}}` — `name` and the outer `sheets` envelope are both required. Agents typically use `df_to_sheet(df, name)` from `scripts/sheets_df.py` to pack each DataFrame into one item, then wrap the list in `{"sheets":[...]}`. Mutually exclusive with --values. Creates the workbook, then writes typed type-faithful data (dates land as real dates, numbers keep precision). (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))
      --styles {styles:[...]}   Initial visual operations as JSON: top-level {styles:[...]}. Each item corresponds to one target sheet and must include `name`, plus at least one of `cell_styles` / `row_sizes` / `col_sizes` / `cell_merges`. `cell_styles` entries use +cells-set-style fields with a cell range; row/col sizes use dimension ranges plus type/size; merges use cell ranges plus optional merge_type. With --sheets, styles array length/order/name must match --sheets.sheets. With --values, pass exactly one styles item for the initial sheet (its name is ignored). (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))
      --title string            Spreadsheet title
      --values [["alice",95]]   Untyped initial data as one 2D JSON array ([["alice",95]]); values are written as-is with their type auto-detected (dates / numbers land as text — use --sheets to preserve types), through the same batched set_cell_range path as --sheets — pair with --styles for number formats, colors, merges, and row/col sizes (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))

Risk: write

Tips:
    • --values is an optional untyped fill (one JSON 2D array). It writes through the same batched set_cell_range path as --sheets; pair it with --styles to set number formats, colors, merges, and row/col sizes. Partial failure leaves the spreadsheet created but empty.
    • --sheets writes typed, type-faithful data (dates → real dates, numbers keep precision) in one step — the create + typed write that +table-put can't do on its own. Mutually exclusive with --values; the new workbook's default sheet becomes the first sheet (no empty Sheet1 left behind).

commands.details:
Export a spreadsheet to xlsx or a single sheet to csv (async + poll + optional download).

Usage:
  lark-cli sheets +workbook-export [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                   identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run                     print request without executing
      --file-extension csv          Export file format; csv mode requires `--sheet-id` (xlsx|csv) (default "xlsx")

  -h, --help                        help for +workbook-export
  -q, --jq string                   jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                        shorthand for --format json
      --output-path ./out.xlsx      Local save path. When omitted, **only the export task is triggered + polled, the file is NOT downloaded** (returns file_token / status so a later step can resume the download). Pass a concrete path (e.g. ./out.xlsx) or a directory (`.` keeps the server-provided filename) to download. Note: the equivalent `lark-cli drive +export --doc-type sheet` uses three separate flags (`--output-dir` / `--file-name` / `--overwrite`) and defaults to downloading into the current directory; this wrapper collapses them into a single `--output-path` for ergonomics but defaults to no-download — fall back to `drive +export` if the split flag set fits better.
      --sheet-id +workbook-export   Required only in csv mode: which sheet to export as CSV. This is a +workbook-export-specific flag, unrelated to the common four-tuple sheet locator (this shortcut does not accept the common sheet locator)
      --spreadsheet-token --url     Spreadsheet token (XOR with --url)
      --url --spreadsheet-token     Spreadsheet URL (XOR with --spreadsheet-token)

Risk: read

Tips:
    • Polls for a bounded window; if the export is still running it returns a resume reference instead of blocking. Pass --output-path to download the file once ready (omit it to only create the export task and get the file token back).

commands.details:
List tasks assigned to me

Usage:
  lark-cli task +get-my-tasks [flags]

Flags:
      --as string           identity type: user
      --complete            if true, query completed tasks;if false, query incompleted tasks; if not provided, both completed and incompleted tasks are queried.
      --created_at string   query tasks created after this time (date/relative/ms)
      --dry-run             print request without executing
      --due-end string      query tasks with due date before this time (date/relative/ms)
      --due-start string    query tasks with due date after this time (date/relative/ms)
      --format string       output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                help for +get-my-tasks
  -q, --jq string           jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                shorthand for --format json
      --page-all            automatically paginate through all pages (max 40)
      --page-limit int      max page limit (default 20, max 40 with --page-all) (default 20)
      --page-token string   start from the specified page token
      --query string        search for tasks by summary (exact match first, then partial match)

Risk: read

complete.description: true, query completed tasks;if false, query incompleted tasks; if not provided, both completed and incompleted tasks are queried.

created_at.description: query tasks created after this time (date/relative/ms)

due-end.description: query tasks with due date before this time (date/relative/ms)

due-start.description: query tasks with due date after this time (date/relative/ms)

format.description: output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")

page-token.description: start from the specified page token

query.description: search for tasks by summary (exact match first, then partial match)

member_value.description: 人员类型的自定义字段值。可以设置1个或多个用户的id（遵循member格式，只支持user类型）。当字段设为只不能多选时只能输入一个值。设为空数组表示设为空

multi_select_value.description: 多选类型字段值，可以填写一个或多个本字段的option_guid。设为空数组表示设为空

number_value.description: 数字类型的自定义字段值，填写一个合法数字的字符串表示，空字符串表示设为空

single_select_value.description: 单选类型字段值，填写一个字段选项的option_guid。设置为空字符串表示设为空

text_value.description: 文本类型字段值。可以填写最多3000字符。使用空字符串表示设为空
text_value.example: 文本类型字段值。可以输入一段文本。空字符串表示清空。

commands.details:
获取会议详情

Risk: read

Full parameter schema:
  lark-cli schema vc.meeting.get

Usage:
  lark-cli vc meeting get [flags]

API Parameters:
  Required:
      --meeting-id string   会议ID（视频会议的唯一标识，视频会议开始后才会产生）
  Optional:
      --query-mode int         此次查询的查询模式，不传，或传0，只查询会议信息. enum: 0=只查询会议信息（默认）|1=只查询会议产物（纪要、逐字稿）
      --user-id-type string    此次调用中使用的用户ID的类型，默认使用open_id可不填. enum: user_id=以user_id来识别用户|union_id=以union_id来识别用户|open_id=以open_id来识别用户（推荐）
      --with-meeting-ability   是否需要会中使用能力统计（仅限tenant_access_token）. bool flag (presence = true; omit for false; takes no value)
      --with-participants      是否需要参会人列表. bool flag (presence = true; omit for false; takes no value)

Raw Parameter Input:
      --params string   Raw URL/query params JSON. Supports - and @file. If both set, typed flags override matching keys in --params.

Execution:
      --as string   identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run     print request without executing

Output:
      --format string   output format: json|ndjson|table|csv (default json)
  -q, --jq string       jq expression to filter JSON output
  -o, --output string   output file path for binary responses

Other:
  -h, --help   help for get
      --json   shorthand for --format json

enumDescriptions: 只查询会议产物（纪要、逐字稿）

  lark-cli wiki +move-to-drive [flags]

Flags:
      --as string             identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run               print request without executing
      --folder-token string   target Drive folder token; omit to move to the calling identity's personal-space root

  -h, --help                  help for +move-to-drive
  -q, --jq string             jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                  shorthand for --format json
      --node-token string     wiki node_token to move out of the knowledge space

Risk: write

Tips:
    • The source must be a wiki node_token, not the backing document's obj_token; use wiki +node-get when unsure.
    • Omit --folder-token to move the document to the calling identity's personal-space root.
    • Moving out of Wiki removes the node from the Wiki tree and replaces inherited Wiki permissions with the target Drive folder's permission model.
    • The move is asynchronous; if the bounded poll times out, continue with the next_command returned in the output.

commands.details:
Delete a wiki node, polling the async delete task when needed

Usage:
  lark-cli wiki +node-delete [flags]

Flags:
      --as string           identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run             print request without executing
      --format string       output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                help for +node-delete
      --include-children    cascade delete the subtree (default); pass --include-children=false to lift direct children up to the parent (default true)
  -q, --jq string           jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                shorthand for --format json
      --node-token string   wiki node_token, cloud-doc obj_token, or a Lark URL embedding one of them
      --obj-type string     token kind; no default — pass explicitly when --node-token is a raw token (URL inputs auto-infer) (wiki|doc|docx|sheet|bitable|mindnote|slides|file)
      --space-id string     wiki space ID; auto-resolved via get_node when omitted
      --yes                 confirm high-risk operation

Risk: high-risk-write

Tips:
    • Deletion is irreversible; double-check --node-token and --obj-type before running.
    • This is a high-risk-write command; pass --yes to confirm the deletion.
    • --node-token accepts a raw token (wikcnXXX, docxXXX, ...) or a Lark URL like https://feishu.cn/wiki/<token> or https://feishu.cn/docx/<token>; URL paths also imply --obj-type.
    • Run +node-get first to confirm space_id / obj_type when in doubt.
    • Auto-resolving space_id (when --space-id is omitted) also calls get_node, which needs the wiki:node:retrieve scope; pass --space-id to skip that lookup if your token only carries wiki:node:create.
    • Async deletes return a task_id; this command polls for a bounded window and then prints a follow-up drive +task_result command.

commands.details:
获取知识空间列表

Risk: read

Full parameter schema:
  lark-cli schema wiki.spaces.list

Usage:
  lark-cli wiki spaces list [flags]

API Parameters:
  Optional:
      --page-size int       分页大小. max: 50. API default: 20
      --page-token string   分页标记，第一次请求不填，表示从头开始遍历

Raw Parameter Input:
      --params string   Raw URL/query params JSON. Supports - and @file. If both set, typed flags override matching keys in --params.

Execution:
      --as string        identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run          print request without executing
      --page-all         automatically paginate through all pages
      --page-delay int   delay in ms between pages (default 200)
      --page-limit int   max pages to fetch with --page-all (0 = unlimited) (default 10)

Output:
      --format string   output format: json|ndjson|table|csv (default json)
  -q, --jq string       jq expression to filter JSON output
  -o, --output string   output file path for binary responses

Other:
  -h, --help   help for list
      --json   shorthand for --format json

page_token.description: 分页标记，第一次请求不填，表示从头开始遍历；分页查询结果还有更多项时会同时返回新的 page_token，下次遍历可采用该 page_token 获取查询结果
